mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined for two consecutive weeks (12.7 to 10.9) as people spend less time at home, a direct inverse signal that discretionary outings including retail and recreation trips will continue to rise over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 12.7 at t-2w to 10.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week improvement in TRANSIT of more than 2 points (from -35.0 to -32.9) signals renewed commuting and errand-running activity that will translate into higher retail footfall within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -35.0 at t-1w to -32.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the subsequent two weeks despite TRANSIT crossing the 2-point weekly improvement threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in both WORKPLACES (stabilizing near -21.9) and TRANSIT (improving to -32.9) jointly indicates resumption of daily commuting routines, and their combined upward movement amplifies retail and recreation mobility beyond what either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show positive week-on-week change simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES flat at -21.9 while TRANSIT improved from -35.0 to -32.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks is no greater than growth predicted from TRANSIT alone, indicating no interaction effect, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint recovery.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility dropped sharply at t-1w (-31.1) likely reflecting a tightening of outdoor gathering restrictions; if such restrictions are reimposed or extended, broader retail and recreation mobility will fall over the following four weeks due to spillover policy effects.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week again
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -20.0 at t-2w to -31.1 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or remains flat over the next four weeks even if PARKS experiences another sharp weekly decline of 10+ points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility stabilizing near baseline (-5.1 at t-0w after a dip to -7.4) suggests households have normalized essential shopping routines, a leading indicator that non-essential retail trips will rise modestly within one week as routine confidence returns.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM recovered from -7.4 at t-1w to -5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the first week following GROCERY_PHARM stabilization within 2 points of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS decline at t-1w followed by partial rebound at t-0w reflects a seasonal weather transition rather than policy change; as seasonal outdoor activity normalizes over the next two weeks, overlapping outdoor-retail behavior will lift RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS partially rebounded from -31.1 at t-1w to -23.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks despite continued PARKS recovery toward baseline.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself rose by 3.8 points in the most recent week (-30.7 to -26.9), and this single-week momentum, if sustained, is a direct autoregressive signal that the series will continue trending upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -30.7 at t-1w to -26.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC reverses and declines over the next four weeks despite the most recent single-week upward momentum.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES recovery stalls (remaining flat near -21.9) while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above 10, this combination signals a partial, incomplete reopening regime in which retail and recreation mobility growth will be capped or reversed over the next four weeks because people retain home-centric routines despite some workplace activity.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays within 1 point of prior week value while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES flat at -21.9 for two consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next four weeks despite WORKPLACES stagnation and persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL readings.
